bull_case_summary: Gamuda has a large construction order book, positive annual profit growth and a constructive trend. Round two acknowledges gearing above the internal limit and conditions the upside on funded backlog conversion and a credible return within that limit.
bear_case_summary: Profit growth lagged revenue, property profit fell and net gearing of 72% exceeded the disclosed 70% limit. Round two accepts that profits remain positive but notes neither backlog nor earnings proves cash conversion capable of repairing leverage.
key_points_of_agreement: The RM61bn order book is a real opportunity rather than a funding solution.
Gearing is above the internal limit and is a concrete thesis gate.
Annual profit growth remains positive but trails revenue.
The positive chart offers no financing protection.
key_points_of_disagreement: How much execution upside remains investable before actual cash conversion and gearing repair appear.
unresolved_uncertainties: Working capital, FCF and funded delivery of the backlog.
Path and timing back within the disclosed gearing limit.
Property earnings recovery and overseas execution.
Matched normalised valuation; JV-inclusive revenue is not a matched consolidated-margin denominator.
